newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian city tense after police clash with Moslems.
newsitem.headline: Indian city tense after police clash with Moslems.

text.p: Some 8,000 police enforced an indefinite curfew in parts of the northern Indian city of Lucknow on Friday after clashes with Moslem marchers led to the detention of some 1,100 people, authorities said.
The violence erupted on Thursday when about 15,000 Shia Moslems defied a 20-year-old ban on religious processions to mark the Chehllum festival.
The ban was imposed in 1977 after about 15 people were killed in clashes between members of the Shia and Sunni sects.

Officials said they feared renewed violence as the curfew would prevent Moslems in the walled old city of Lucknow, capital of the northern state of Uttar Pradesh, from going to their mosques for Friday prayers.

On Thursday, irate marchers threw stones at police and set six shops, a bus and a three-wheeler vehicle on fire. Two marchers were injured when police fired warning shots to disperse the crowd, authorities said.
Police said there were some clashes between the rival Shias and Sunnis.
Police said 12 people were taken to hospital, including seven police, but that dozens more may have been treated at home. The Press Trust of India put the number of injured at about 50.
Authorities imposed an indefinite curfew in six police station areas covering about one third of the city.

"We cannot permit people to step out of their houses, considering how they went berserk defying prohibitory orders and fighting pitched battles with the police yesterday," the new district magistrate, J.S. Mishra, told Reuters.
Mishra took charge late on Thursday after the authorities, angry over the outbreak of violence, sacked his predecessor.
